changes.before: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October indicates that economic activity is expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.after: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that growth in economic activity picked up in recent quarters.

changes.before: Labor market conditions have shown further improvement; the unemployment rate has declined but remains elevated.
changes.after: Labor market indicators were mixed but on balance showed further improvement.

changes.before: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, while the recovery in the housing sector slowed somewhat in recent months.
changes.after: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced more quickly in recent months, while the recovery in the housing sector slowed somewhat.

changes.before: Fiscal policy is restraining economic growth, although the extent of restraint may be diminishing.
changes.after: Fiscal policy is restraining economic growth, although the extent of restraint is diminishing.

changes.before: the Committee decided to modestly reduce the pace of its asset purchases. Beginning in January, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $35 billion per month rather than $40 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $40 billion per month rather than $45 billion per month.
changes.after: the Committee decided to make a further measured reduction in the pace of its asset purchases. Beginning in February, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $30 billion per month rather than $35 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $35 billion per month rather than $40 billion per month.

changes.before: economic growth will pick up from its recent pace
changes.after: economic activity will expand at a moderate pace

changes.before: Voting against the action was Eric S. Rosengren, who believes that, with the unemployment rate still elevated and the inflation rate well below the target, changes in the purchase program are premature until incoming data more clearly indicate that economic growth is likely to be sustained above its potential rate.

parsed.rationale: The Committee continued tapering by another $10 billion, upgraded its growth assessment, and was unanimous with the dovish dissent dropped, while leaving forward guidance on rates unchanged. This is a modest hawkish shift, consistent with the expected path rather than a change in direction.

spans.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October indicates that economic activity is expanding at a moderate pace.
Labor market conditions have shown further improvement; the unemployment rate has declined but remains elevated.
Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, while the recovery in the housing sector slowed somewhat in recent months.
Fiscal policy is restraining economic growth, although the extent of restraint may be diminishing.

the Committee decided to modestly reduce the pace of its asset purchases. Beginning in January, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $35 billion per month rather than $40 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $40 billion per month rather than $45 billion per month.
economic growth will pick up from its recent pace

Voting against the action was Eric S. Rosengren, who believes that, with the unemployment rate still elevated and the inflation rate well below the target, changes in the purchase program are premature until incoming data more clearly indicate that economic growth is likely to be sustained above its potential rate.
Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that growth in economic activity picked up in recent quarters.
Labor market indicators were mixed but on balance showed further improvement.
Household spending and business fixed investment advanced more quickly in recent months, while the recovery in the housing sector slowed somewhat.
Fiscal policy is restraining economic growth, although the extent of restraint is diminishing.

the Committee decided to make a further measured reduction in the pace of its asset purchases. Beginning in February, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $30 billion per month rather than $35 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $35 billion per month rather than $40 billion per month.
economic activity will expand at a moderate pace
